ambiguities.text: The term 'major client implementations' is not precisely defined - unclear which clients qualify and what percentage of network hashpower/stake they must represent.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'major clients' means at least 3 of the main execution clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) that together represent >80% of network participation.

ambiguities.text: The process for handling emergency security patches that need rapid deployment is not addressed.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume emergency fixes can bypass the standard timeline through an expedited All Core Devs decision, but this needs separate documentation.

ambiguities.text: The meaning of 'soft deadline' for implementations is unclear - what happens if the deadline is missed?
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume soft deadline means the EIP may be excluded from the hard fork if implementations are not ready, but exceptions can be made case-by-case.

implicit_assumptions.description: The All Core Devs group acts in good faith and makes decisions that benefit the Ethereum network as a whole.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious or captured governance could lead to inclusion of harmful changes or exclusion of necessary security fixes.

implicit_assumptions.description: Client teams have sufficient resources to implement approved EIPs within the specified timeline.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Hard fork delays, rushed implementations, or incomplete testing could introduce bugs or security vulnerabilities.

implicit_assumptions.description: The majority of the network (miners/validators and users) will upgrade their clients before the activation block.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Chain split risk if significant portion of network doesn't upgrade, potentially leading to double-spend attacks during the split.
